analysis:
Both changed files are test-only: CoordinatorIntegrationTests.swift and the new CoordinatorReconnectPolicyTests.swift. No production code, no keys, no attestation or authorization logic, and no cache storage code changed in the supplied units.

In CoordinatorIntegrationTests.swift the head side makes four changes. The header comments now say the suite runs in CI instead of being skipped (head lines 10-12, 21). makeClient gains a reconnectPolicy parameter (head 649-677). New helpers reregistrationTime and withGrownReconnectBackoff (head 679-727) drive the mock coordinator. Two new tests (head 456-490) check that a 1012 close reconnects within 1 s and that a stable session resets the backoff.

The tests use a loopback MockCoordinator with fake signatures and generated keys, so no secrets are involved.

The suite is now meant to run in CI, which is a test-coverage improvement and not a security regression. The test comments cite only the reconnect policy and do not touch any threat-model control.

The reconnect behavior being tested (CoordinatorReconnectPolicy, a 0-1 s jittered wait for close code 1012, no backoff growth) lives in production code that is not in the supplied units, so I could not review it. A coordinator-triggered 1012 gives a faster reconnect without backoff growth, so a coordinator or an adversary able to inject close frames could cause reconnect storms. Both are plausible availability questions (TB-002), but the policy implementation is not in the supplied evidence, so I record it as an unverified contract and not as a finding.

The new test file CoordinatorReconnectPolicyTests.swift was provided only as metadata and a truncated patch excerpt, with no numbered source text. I did not see its full contents.

Remaining question for integration: whether the production reconnect policy (outside this batch) bounds the 1012 fast path, for example with a cap on rapid repeated 1012 closes, and whether re-registration after a reconnect still requires the full attestation and authorization re-grant described in T-053.
